title: Inspect this page: What's On at the SU
brief:
The students' union has made a bright poster of a page for this week's events. It looks great. Five things on it make it hard for some people to use: two you have found before, three are new kinds of problem. Find them. Tick each one you find and write one sentence saying why it matters for a real user. Not every item in the list is a real problem on this page, so look before you tick.

To look at the real HTML: right-click anything on the sample page and choose Inspect. The browser's developer tools open and show the tag under your mouse.

vocabulary.gloss: words that describe an image for people who cannot see it; a file name is not a description
the words inside … ; they should say where the link goes
about 1 in 12 men and 1 in 200 women cannot tell some colours apart, most often red and green
grey text inside a box that disappears when you type; it is not a label

problems.label: The picture's alt text is a file name, not a description
problems.why: A screen reader reads the alt text aloud, so the listener hears "IMG 4471 jpg" and learns nothing about the picture.

problems.label: A link's text is only "click here"
problems.why: Screen-reader users often jump from link to link; "click here" on its own does not say where the link goes, and it is slower for everyone scanning the page.

problems.label: Some text is far too small (10px)
problems.why: Small print is hard for everyone and impossible for many people with low vision, and it hides the conditions people need to know.

problems.label: Whether an event has tickets is shown only by a coloured dot
problems.why: Anyone who cannot tell the two colours apart, and anyone using a screen reader, gets no information: the word "sold out" is needed too.

problems.label: A form input has no label
problems.why: Placeholder text disappears when you type and is not read reliably; a label says what the box is for.

problems.label: A button is made from a <div>, not a <button>

hints: Two of the five are things you have found before: a form box, and a picture. But this time read the alt text itself: right-click the picture, choose Inspect, and look at alt="…".
Two are about text: one link and one paragraph. Read the link out loud without the words around it. Can you read the small print at the bottom without leaning in?
The last one is about colour: what do the green and red dots in the list mean, and where does the page tell you? Real problems: 5; the other two items in the list are not true here.
